summary: Do not ship: the diff violates the single-flip release contract, and its central KubeJobFailed regression test passes using an impossible future timestamp.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Open question: two independent behavior flips lack the required approval
findings.body: The diagnosis explicitly identifies KubeJobFailed suppression and GHA age-budget changes as independent observable flips, then requires Stage 2 to stop for a user decision. No decisions.md exists, yet both changes are present. This violates the release rubric and couples unrelated verification and rollback surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Split the fixes into independently releasable changes, or record explicit authorization to reclassify the work as /feature or /deepen with separate verification and rollback criteria for both flips.

findings.title: The recovery regression test injects a future success outside its replay window
findings.body: L1 uses a 3,600-second recovery lag, but the replay spans only 2,700 seconds (`3 × for:15m`). It nevertheless emits `last_ok = job_start + resolve_lag` at every sample, so the alleged success is 900 seconds after replay completion and is visible retroactively from the first evaluation. Requiring zero historical firing therefore validates an impossible KSM timeline rather than failure-then-recovery behavior; the release's primary regression evidence can pass without exercising the real transition.
findings.recommendation: Model last-success as the previous value until an in-window recovery, then switch it at the recovery timestamp. Assert firing before recovery and resolution afterward, or place both failure and recovery before replay start when testing an already-resolved stale Job.
